title: Letter Case Permutation
statement: The string `s` is made of letters and digits. Each letter may be written either in lowercase or in uppercase, chosen independently of the others, while digits never change. Return every distinct string that can be produced this way, in any order.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters, uppercase English letters and digits
notes:
## Intuition

Each letter is an independent two-way choice and each digit has only one option, so the answers are the leaves of a binary decision tree over the letters. With `k` letters there are exactly `2^k` distinct strings. Enumerating all `2^k` bitmasks over the letter positions works too; backtracking builds the same strings by walking the tree one position at a time.

## Approach

1. Copy `s` into a mutable array `chars` and start an empty `result`.
2. `backtrack(index)` decides the character at `index`. When `index` reaches the end, join `chars` and record the string.
3. A digit has nothing to choose: move straight to `index + 1`.
4. A letter branches twice: set it to lowercase and recurse, then set it to uppercase and recurse.
5. Restore the original character before returning so the caller sees `chars` unchanged.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "a1b2"`. At index 0 the letter `a` branches. On the lowercase branch, index 1 is the digit `1` (no choice), index 2 is `b`: lowercase gives `"a1b2"`, uppercase gives `"a1B2"` once the digit `2` is passed. Back at index 0, the uppercase branch repeats this and records `"A1b2"` and `"A1B2"`. The result is `["a1b2","a1B2","A1b2","A1B2"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(2^k · n): there are `2^k` leaves and each join costs O(n).
- Space: O(n) for `chars` and the recursion depth, plus the O(2^k · n) output.

## Pitfalls

- Branching on digits doubles the work and produces duplicate strings.
- An input letter may already be uppercase; set both cases explicitly instead of "flipping" it, or you can miss or repeat a case.
- Forgetting to restore `chars[index]` leaks one branch's choice into the next.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | every completed string |
| `chars` | the string being built, edited in place |
| `index` | the position currently being decided |
| `ch` | the original character at `index` |

narration.3: Turn the string into an array so single characters can be changed in place.
narration.5: backtrack decides the character at index, then hands the rest to deeper calls.
narration.7: ...so record the current string as one answer.
narration.10: Remember the original character so it can be restored afterwards.
narration.11: Digits have only one form, so there is nothing to choose.

narration.15: First branch: write this letter in lowercase.
narration.16: Decide all the remaining positions with the lowercase choice.
narration.17: Second branch: write the same letter in uppercase.
narration.18: Decide all the remaining positions with the uppercase choice.
